 1. Original Work 
 Projects submitted to CodeSprint should be created specifically for the challenge.
 Existing projects may be used as inspiration or as a starting point only where explicitly permitted, but participants should clearly disclose any pre-existing code, components, libraries, APIs, datasets, or other materials used.
 2. Open Source 
 Projects must have a public GitHub repository and should include an appropriate open-source license.
 3. Team Size 
 Teams may consist of 5  members .
 All team members must be listed on the Devpost submission.
 4. AI Tools 
 AI-assisted development tools are allowed. Participants remain responsible for their submissions and should comply with the terms of any tools, APIs, datasets, or third-party services they use.
 5. Third-Party Tools & APIs 
 Participants may use publicly available libraries, frameworks, APIs, datasets, and development tools, subject to their respective licenses and terms.
 6. Submission Deadline 
 All online project submissions must be completed by 15 November 2026 .
 Late submissions may not be considered for the final shortlist.
 7. Final Pitch 
 Shortlisted finalists must be available for the offline final pitch in Dehradun on 22 November 2026 .
 8. Code of Conduct 
 All participants are expected to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and professional environment throughout the event.
 Harassment, discrimination, hate speech, threats, cheating, plagiarism, or malicious activity will not be tolerated.
 9. Intellectual Property 
 Participants retain ownership of their projects and intellectual property, subject to the licenses and terms applicable to any third-party components they use.
 10. Disqualification 
 Organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules, contain plagiarized work, misrepresent contributions, or violate applicable laws or third-party terms.
